I am here in Mtwara, and my maize plot is 1.30 hectares on my own land. The soil here is sandy and tired, and the rains do not always come well. I have some schooling so I can read the bag, but cash is tight — my husband and I mostly rely on what we harvest and a little from cashew. Last season I did not use chemical fertilizer because the bag was too expensive at the dukani, and most of my neighbors here also plant maize without it. This year I will do the same as last year — plant local seed I kept from last harvest, put some manure from our few goats and chickens, and weed carefully with my children. I cannot risk buying fertilizer when the rain is uncertain; if the season fails I still need to feed my family.
